title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel / disconnect / reconnect / server timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: streaming endpoints (chat/generation/func-call) historically had inconsistent behavior when clients cancel or disconnect mid-stream and when clients reconnect to resume a stream. This resulted in leaked in-flight resources, duplicated events on reconnect, and occasional 504s when server-side timeouts raced with client disconnects. This PR implements a holistic lifecycle control surface to make the streaming behavior predictable and compatible with our OpenAI-compatible adapter. Key changes: (1) explicit client-cancel semantics: support for HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and SSE/HTTP streaming client disconnect detection mapped to a unified Cancel event in the runtime; (2) reconnect & resume tokens: short-lived resume tokens emitted as part of the stream metadata which allow idempotent resume from last acknowledged token; (3) server-side idle and max-response timeouts: server will emit a final Timeout event and release KV cache and execution slots gracefully; (4) heartbeats and client acking: optional heartbeat messages to differentiate network blips from client intent to cancel; (5) ordering & dedup guarantees for OpenAI-compatible deltas and function call events to avoid duplicate tool invocations on resume; (6) observability and testing: new metrics (stream_resume_attempts, stream_cancels, stream_timeouts) and an end-to-end test harness to reproduce disconnect+resume scenarios. The description below is a single continuous string and includes rationale, checklist, and links. Related: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7890, internal runbook: docs/runbooks/streaming-reconnect.md. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by runtime/APIs - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] OpenAI-compat adapter updated - [x] e2e reconnect/resume scenario validated against quickstart example - [x] metrics and alerts added to Redwood Console

notes_for_release_notes: Improve streaming stability: client cancel and disconnect are now handled deterministically, support for reconnect/resume with short-lived resume tokens, server-side timeouts emit explicit Timeout events, new metrics for stream lifecycle (stream_resume_attempts, stream_cancels, stream_timeouts). OpenAI-compat adapter emits resume-token header and preserves delta ordering to avoid duplicate function calls on resume.
tests_added: e2e: examples/quickstarts/streaming_resume.ts run in CI matrix
observability_changes: logs: lifecycle.trace includes resume_token and finalization_state
upgrade_notes: No breaking API changes. If you relied on implicit behavior where disconnect always aborted without a final event, note that server now emits an explicit Timeout/Cancel final event and releases slots more promptly. Resume tokens are opt-in via the stream config and default to 60s TTL.
security_considerations: Added rate limits and GC for resume state to mitigate abuse. Resume tokens are single-use and signed by the control plane. Tokens expire after configured TTL. Audit logs include resume token issuance and resume attempts when audit-level logging is enabled.

notes: This PR stitches together runtime, adapter, and API docs. Implementation choices (short-lived resume tokens + idempotent slot finalization) were driven by production incidents where leaked slots caused tail latency regressions. See docs/runbooks/streaming-reconnect.md for incident reproduction steps.
